transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Raman (CTO - Elysium), Carlos Mendes (ML Eng), Aisha Khan (Head of Data)

Summary (auto):
- POC scoping for open-model shortlist and benchmark plan for diagnostics NLP tasks.
- Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination, latency), workload sizing, timeline for bench and pilot, and security/compliance constraints (PHI, VPC/KMS).
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to run benchmark on 3 open-model variants, customer to provide sample data and confirm PHI scope, follow-up in 2 weeks.

Topics: open-model selection, quantization tradeoffs, multilingual support (Spanish/Arabic), domain adaptation, benchmark metrics, Dedicated vs Private deployment, timeline and acceptance criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jasmine from Redwood, this is Marcus our SE, we'll run through POC scope for open models for the diagnostics workflows. Priya, do you want to kick off with goals?
[00:12] Dr. Priya Raman: Sure thanks. Our main goal is to replace a manual triage/annotation step in the intake pipeline, so we need high recall for entities and few hallucinations. Performance wise we'd like p95 latency under 400 to 600 ms for typical requests, and cost needs to be sustainable for a production roll out. We also have multilingual notes (Spanish + Portuguese) and some Portuguese/Arabic later this year.
[00:37] Carlos: to add, volume is currently about 25k requests/day peak-ish, average prompt length ~120 tokens, expected response ~160 tokens, plus lots of short queries for triage.
[00:48] Marcus: got it, so roughly sizing wise that's ~25k * (120+160)=7 million tokens/day, ballpark. That maps into throughput and cost planning. We'll include both latency and batch throughput in our bench.
[01:05] Aisha: important: this data has PHI, so we need either Private deployment or a contract that explicitly covers PHI handling. We have to follow our legal and security regs.
[01:16] Jasmine: understoood, PHI is an important constraint. For the POC we can run in Redwood Dedicated or Private; Dedicated can be in a customer VPC with KMS integration, or Private for on-prem. We'll detail options in the follow-up.
[01:29] Speaker 1: quick Q on success metrics. Do we have specific thresholds for accuracy? F1?
[01:34] Dr. Priya Raman: We're aiming for >0.85 F1 on entity extraction on our validation set, hallucination rate under 2% for structured outputs, and human eval score >4/5 for triage suggestions. If models can't meet that, we'll consider finetuning/adapter strategy.
[01:50] Marcus: ok that's helpful. For open-model shortlist we recommend testing a mix of architectures and sizes: Llama-3-13B quantized (q4_q8 variants), Mistral-Instruct-16B, and Falcon-40B-instruct q8 as a heavier baseline. We'll also try a distilled smaller model for latency-sensitive paths (e.g., MPT-7B-instruct).
[02:15] Carlos: do you have any evidence on domain performance? Historically Llama variants have been strong on instruction tasks but medical terminology sometimes trips things up.
[02:24] Marcus: yep, domain gaps are real. We'll run our standard eval including entity F1 and a hallucination detection recipe. For models that miss targets, we can recommend lightweight finetune or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with your knowledge base.
[02:36] Jasmine: timeline-wise, can we confirm sample data availability? Marcus needs ~500 labeled prompts + ground truth to run initial bench. Carlos?
[02:44] Carlos: I can upload 500 prompts by Wednesday, 2026-03-25. Some labels are noisy but it's okay for initial runs.
[02:51] Aisha: on security, please share your SOC2 and encryption docs. We need KMS instructions for key rotation and SIEM integration for audit logs.
[02:58] Jasmine: will do, I have the security pack link and we'll attach the KMS integration guide. Link (note): https://redwood.ai/security/poc-pack and the bench spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/sheets/elysium-poc-bench (we'll populate).
[03:13] Dr. Priya Raman: curious about quantization — you mentioned q4/q8. For us latency matters but we also need minimal quality loss for medical entities, any guidance?
[03:22] Marcus: generally q8 gives a nice middle ground for larger models — better latency and memory with small quality degradation; q4 can be useful for 13B-class models when you need very low memory usage. We'll include both q4_0 and q8 runs in the benchmark so you can see tradeoffs.
[03:35] Carlos: and what about multilingual? Will the open models handle Spanish/Portuguese? We have specific dialects.
[03:42] Marcus: some models have stronger multilingual pretraining — Mistral variants often handle Western European languages well, Llama-3 has improved multilingual coverage over Llama-2, but we should run per-language evaluations. If performance is poor we can do adapter finetuning or use RAG with translated KBs.
[03:58] Speaker 2: any hard SLA needs for POC?
[04:02] Aisha: for the POC we need p95 latency under 600 ms on Dedicated. Production targets are stricter, but POC safety buffer okay.
[04:09] Jasmine: noted. On Redwood side we'll provision a Dedicated pool sized for your traffic for bench runs; that will approximate production. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens in the report.
[04:22] Marcus: quick note on benchmarking methodology: we'll run cold and warm cache scenarios, and with batching enabled at different batch sizes; also measure KV-cache hit effects for multi-step dialogs if you have those.
[04:34] Dr. Priya Raman: we do have multi-step follow ups for some triage flows, so KV cache is relevant.
[04:39] Marcus: ok we'll include a short multi-turn bench as well.
[04:43] Jasmine: any procurement/legal blockers we should be aware of?
[04:46] Aisha: we'll need a Data Processing Addendum and to verify encryption at rest/in transit. Also on contract side, limited indemnity for PHI.
[04:56] Jasmine: we'll loop Legal and share standard DPA template and SOC2 reports.
[04:59] Speaker 1: can you outline acceptance criteria so stakeholders are aligned?
[05:02] Dr. Priya Raman: Acceptance: Entity F1 >=0.85, hallucination <2%, p95 latency <400 ms on production target config, cost per 1M tokens under $X (TBD after you provide cost calc). Also security approvals completed.
[05:19] Marcus: we'll populate cost estimate; for bench we'll use internal metrics but we'll show extrapolated 1M-token cost for each model and quant.
[05:27] Carlos: about pilot timeline — if bench looks good, how long to spin a pilot?
[05:31] Jasmine: typical pilot is 6 weeks: 2 weeks bench & validation, 2 weeks integration with your pipeline and fine-tuning if needed, 2 weeks user acceptance & metrics review. If you need deeper compliance work for on-prem, add 2-4 weeks.
[05:47] Aisha: that's reasonable. We have a Q3 launch target for a limited feature, so POC + pilot needs to finish by end of May ideally.
[05:56] Jasmine: so target: bench complete by early April, pilot start mid-April, pilot complete by end-May — we'll align dates in follow-up.
[06:05] Marcus: for the bench models I'll run these configurations: Llama-3-13B (q4 and q8), Mistral-Instruct-16B (float16 plus q8), Falcon-40B-instruct q8, and MPT-7B-instruct as low-latency option. We'll report accuracy, hallucination rate, latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost.
[06:25] Dr. Priya Raman: will you also include a run with retrieval augmented generation?
[06:29] Marcus: yes we'll do a RAG-config run using a simple vector store of your KB to show improvements on domain-specific questions.
[06:35] Carlos: one more — for multilingual tests, can we include Spanish and Portuguese subsets of the 500 prompts?
[06:40] Aisha: yes I'll coordinate labels for that subset.
[06:44] Jasmine: great. Quick note: some transcription glitches in the automated notes may mislabel product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Dedicated), apologies if that shows up.
[06:55] Dr. Priya Raman: ha no worries.
[06:58] Jasmine: Recap: Redwood to run benchmark across 3-4 models and quant variants, provision Dedicated pool for bench, share bench spreadsheet and cost calc, send security pack and DPA, customer to upload 500 labeled prompts and confirm PHI scope. Follow-up in 2 weeks to review results.
[07:18] Marcus: action items repeated: I'll start bench runs as soon as the data is uploaded; Marcus will post preliminary numbers to the shared sheet.
[07:27] Carlos: I'll get the data uploaded by 2026-03-25.
[07:31] Aisha: I'll confirm PHI scope and whether we need on-prem by 2026-03-26.
[07:36] Jasmine: ok thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invite for the follow-up.
[07:40] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: ASR had typical speaker splitting errors and occasional word swaps (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'kay-vee cache' once).
